messages:
Anika (SRE): Quick thread — linked the postmortem here https://redwood.pm/postmortem/2827-cascade. Summary: multi-region routing flap cascaded into slow snapshot restores and partial KV cache divergence. I pulled out recurring patterns and suspected runbook gaps. Can we triage into discrete tickets and owners?
Sam (Infra): I skimmed. two quick asks: 1) we need proof-of-restore step in the runbook (we had no fast validation), 2) routing tool fallback didn't surface which routes failed.
Raj (Platform): Hypothesis: route controller retries + delayed control-plane writes caused overlapping cutovers. We should tag routing decisions with request_id and region_hint so traces show the decision path.
Mia (Product): From a customer-impact POV: SEs reported degraded API success rates for ~7m across EU customers. Can we commit an SLA postmortem blurb and timeline?
Leo (Eng): Proposed concrete items: - add runbook check "snapshot-verify" (script below) - instrument route-controller for decision reasons - add chaos test for snapshot restore latency
Leo (Eng): ```bash
# quick verify snapshot restore
./tools/verify_snapshot.sh --region eu-west --snapshot-id $SNAP_ID --target ./tmp/restore && curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/health || echo FAILED
```
Anika (SRE): Good. I'll convert these into tickets but want owners and dates. Suggested minimal grouping: A) Runbook + verification (owner Leo), B) Routing decision tracing (owner Raj), C) Game-day dry-run + chaos (owner Sam), D) Backups SLA + audit (owner Mia). Thoughts?
Sam (Infra): I'm happy to own C. propose dry-run window Wed Apr 14 09:00 PT. Will coordinate on-call rotation. :calendar:
Raj (Platform): I'll take B. For tracing we should add a small header x-rdw-route-id and ensure it's preserved through proxy hops. I'll draft RFC and link infra changes.
Mia (Product): I'll own D (backup SLA + audit) and draft the customer timeline blurb. Target EOD next Tue for the blurb.
Leo (Eng): I'll own A, but need a checklist and CI gating so we don't regress. I'll create a validation job and gate on green.
Anika (SRE): Great. Two more cross-cutting asks: 1) detection: add a recurring metric for cross-region restore latency (percentiles) and alert when p95 > 30s, 2) post-game-day retro slot on calendar.
Sam (Infra): Agreed on alerting. I'll add alert RDW-ALERT-restore-latency and a dashboard tile.
ops-bot: Created ticket RDW-4321: runbook/restore-verification (assignee: Leo).
deploy-bot: Created ticket RDW-4322: routing-trace-instrumentation (assignee: Raj).
Anika (SRE): I'll open a tracker doc and link tickets: https://redwood.docs/trackers/2827-cascade-docket. Please update your ticket's acceptance criteria with the small success checks (restore verification script returns 0, route trace shows route_id).
Mia (Product): Quick note — include a line in the customer blurb that we ran a dry-run within 2 weeks and validated restores. That makes the messaging concrete.
Leo (Eng): On acceptance: will add an automated verify_snapshot CI step that runs weekly and reports to the dashboard.
Raj (Platform): RFC incoming by EOD today. I'll propose header name: X-RDW-ROUTE (string).
Anika (SRE): Thanks all — owners and dates: A (Leo) ticket RDW-4321 due by 2026-04-10, B (Raj) RDW-4322 due 2026-04-03, C (Sam) dry-run 2026-04-14, D (Mia) blurb 2026-03-31. I'll follow up with a short 15m sync tomorrow to unblock any cross-dependencies. :thumbsup:
Sam (Infra): :thumbsup:
Mia (Product): ack
Leo (Eng): ack
Raj (Platform): ack
ops-bot: Ticket RDW-4323 created for game-day coordination (owner: Sam, due: 2026-04-14).
Anika (SRE): Closing note — pattern hypothesis to track across future incidents: "partial restore + routing decision mismatch". If we see this twice more, escalate to a resilience epic. For now, let's get the docket turned into deliverables.
